intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Best Hypoallergenic Dog Breeds
intro.html:
No dog breed is completely allergen-free — the term "hypoallergenic" is technically a misnomer. Dog allergies are primarily triggered not by fur itself but by a protein called Can f 1, which is found in dog saliva, urine, and dander (dead skin cells). All dogs produce these proteins to some degree. Certain breeds shed minimally, so they leave less loose hair around the house. But studies that measured Can f 1 have not found consistently lower allergen levels in homes with so-called hypoallergenic breeds, and one found higher levels in their hair and coats than in control breeds (Vredegoor et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012; Nicholas et al., Am J Rhinol Allergy 2011). For the millions of people who want a dog but struggle with allergies, these low-shedding breeds are a reasonable place to start looking, not a guarantee.

The breeds most commonly described as hypoallergenic tend to share certain coat characteristics. Many have hair rather than fur — a distinction that matters because hair grows in longer cycles and sheds far less continuously than the double coats common in heavy-shedding breeds. Others, like the Xoloitzcuintli (Mexican Hairless), have minimal or no coat at all, so there is little hair to shed, though their skin and saliva still carry allergens like any dog's. Curly-coated breeds like the Poodle and Lagotto Romagnolo tend to hold loose hair in their curls rather than dropping it around the house, although one of the studies above found no difference in airborne allergen levels between breeds.

It's important for anyone with dog allergies to spend time with a specific dog of the breed they're considering before bringing one home. Reactions can vary significantly between individual dogs even within the same breed, and personal sensitivity levels differ widely. Regular grooming, bathing, and vacuuming also play a significant role in managing allergens in the home. Because a breed label alone does not predict allergen levels, talk to an allergist before committing, and pair that advice with a proactive approach to cleanliness.

care.heading: Top Hypoallergenic Dog Breeds
care.html:
Standard Poodle

Large60–90 min10–18 yrs lifespan

The Poodle's curly, non-shedding coat made it a popular choice for those with allergies, but the breed's intelligence and trainability are equally impressive. Originally a water retriever, the Standard Poodle is one of the most capable and adaptable breeds across dog sports, therapy work, and family life.

Full guide →

Portuguese Water Dog

Medium60–90 min11–13 yrs lifespan

The Portuguese Water Dog's wavy or curly coat sheds minimally, making it a popular choice for allergy sufferers. Bred to work alongside fishermen off the Portuguese coast, they are athletic, intelligent, and highly trainable with a strong affinity for water and an enthusiastic work ethic.

Full guide →

Bichon Frise

Small30 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Bichon Frise's fluffy white coat sheds minimally, making it one of the most popular low-shedding small breeds. Cheerful, adaptable, and endlessly affectionate, Bichons are ideal companions for apartment dwellers and families who want a social, low-shedding dog.

Full guide →

Maltese

Small20–30 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Maltese's long, silky coat is single-layered and sheds almost nothing, making it a favorite with owners who want minimal dog hair at home. This ancient companion breed from Malta has been prized for centuries for its gentle, affectionate temperament and manageable size in any living environment.

Full guide →

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier

Medium45–60 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Wheaten's soft, silky coat sheds minimally compared to most dogs, making it a practical choice for owners who want less hair around the house. An all-purpose Irish farm dog, Wheatens balance terrier energy and independence with genuine affection and an adaptable temperament suited to active families.

Full guide →

Kerry Blue Terrier

MediumHigh12–15 yr lifespan

The Kerry Blue's distinctive wavy coat is low-shedding, making it a reasonable breed for allergy sufferers to consider. Ireland's national dog is intelligent, loyal, and versatile—formerly used for herding, hunting, and retrieving across the Irish countryside.

Full guide →

Lagotto Romagnolo

Medium60–90 min15–17 yrs lifespan

The Lagotto's thick, curly coat is woolly in texture and sheds very little, making it one of the lower-shedding medium breeds. Originally bred as a water retriever in the Italian Romagna region, they are now world-famous as truffle hunters, combining an extraordinary nose with eager trainability.

Full guide →

Spanish Water Dog

Medium60–90 min12–14 yrs lifespan

The Spanish Water Dog's curly, woolly coat forms natural cords that are low-shedding, though in one study homes with Spanish Water Dogs had no lower allergen levels than homes with other breeds (Vredegoor et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012). A versatile working breed from the Iberian Peninsula used for herding, hunting, and fishing assistance. Athletic, intelligent, and loyal to their family.

Full guide →

Xoloitzcuintli

Toy / Mini / Standard30–60 min13–18 yrs lifespan

The Xolo is one of the world's oldest and rarest breeds, and the hairless variety has no coat to shed, though like every dog it still produces allergens in its skin and saliva. Mexico's national dog comes in three sizes and two varieties—hairless and coated—and is a loyal, calm, and dignified companion.

Full guide →

Chinese Crested

MediumModerate13–18 yr lifespan

The hairless Chinese Crested has almost no body coat to shed, making it a fixture on hypoallergenic breed lists, though no breed is allergen-free. Affectionate and social, they form close bonds with their owners. The hairless variety requires sunscreen and skin care, while the Powder Puff has a full soft coat.

Full guide →

Also Worth Considering: Designer Crossbreeds

Doodle hybrids are a popular low-shedding option for households that want a friendly retriever- or herding-type temperament with a Poodle coat. Coat outcomes vary by generation - F1B and multigen produce the most reliably low-shedding dogs, while F1 outcomes are unpredictable. All six doodle hybrids covered on Wooffy:

  • Goldendoodle — Golden Retriever x Poodle. Friendly, trainable, often low-shedding.
  • Labradoodle — Labrador Retriever x Poodle. The original designer doodle, energetic and adaptable.
  • Bernedoodle — Bernese Mountain Dog x Poodle. Gentle-giant temperament with reduced shedding.
  • Cavapoo — Cavalier King Charles Spaniel x Poodle. Small, calm, excellent for apartments.
  • Sheepadoodle — Old English Sheepdog x Poodle. Playful and sturdy with a panda coat.
  • Aussiedoodle — Australian Shepherd x Poodle. High-energy, brilliant, often heterochromatic eyes.

See our full Best Doodle Breeds for Families guide for in-depth coverage of all six doodle hybrids.

special.label: Considerations
special.heading: How to Choose the Right Hypoallergenic Breed
special.html:
Before selecting a hypoallergenic breed, it is essential to assess the severity of your allergies. In one study, differences in coat allergen between breeds were small compared with differences between individual dogs of the same breed (Vredegoor et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012), so even people with very mild sensitivity should meet the specific dog first, while those with more significant reactions should consider spending time with multiple dogs of their preferred breed before committing. Visiting a breeder or reputable rescue and spending an hour or two around the dogs — ideally in an indoor setting — can give you a good indication of how your body responds. Consult with an allergist if you are unsure about the severity of your dog allergy.

Grooming is a critical consideration for hypoallergenic breeds. The tradeoff for a low-shedding coat is often more intensive grooming requirements. Poodles, Bichon Frises, and Maltese need professional grooming every 6–8 weeks to prevent matting and maintain coat health. Portuguese Water Dogs and Lagotto Romagnolos need regular brushing at home. Hairless breeds like the Xolo and Chinese Crested require skin care including moisturizer and sun protection. Factor the cost and time of grooming into your decision — it is a real and ongoing expense with most low-shedding breeds.

Think about temperament and lifestyle compatibility alongside allergen concerns. A Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier's low-shedding coat won't help if the dog's high energy doesn't match your lifestyle. A Spanish Water Dog needs a job or sport to stay mentally satisfied. The Maltese and Chinese Crested are better suited to quiet households than active families. Use a breed's low-shedding coat as a filter, not the sole criterion — the right dog for your life is one that matches both your allergy needs and your activity level, living situation, and desire for companionship.

Gear worth having

Low-shedding and long-coated breeds trade vacuuming for brushing. The home kit that keeps professional grooms from turning into shave-downs is a pin brush, a steel comb to check down to the skin, and a detangling spray used before brushing.

  • Chris Christensen Oval Pin Brush (27 mm) on Amazon. Chris Christensen's Original Series oval pin brush: 27 mm stainless pins without ball tips in a cushioned pad, made for long, silky and double coats. Brush in layers from the skin out; a pin brush is for daily maintenance, not for working out mats.
  • Chris Christensen 000 Butter Comb (7.5 in, fine/coarse) on Amazon. A 7.5-inch greyhound-style steel comb with coarse teeth on one half and fine on the other, for checking down to the skin after brushing. Work in sections and stop at resistance; a comb finds mats, it shouldn't be used to rip them out.
  • Chris Christensen Ice on Ice Detangling Spray (16 oz) on Amazon. A leave-in detangling spray with sunscreen, misted on before brushing so the pins slide through the coat instead of tearing it. Mist the coat lightly, not the skin; it's a finishing spray, not a substitute for a bath.

faq.q: Is there truly a 100% hypoallergenic dog?
faq.a: No — every dog produces the Can f 1 protein that triggers most human dog allergies, found in saliva, urine, and dander. Low-shedding breeds leave less loose hair around the house, but studies that measured Can f 1 have not found consistently lower allergen levels in homes with so-called hypoallergenic breeds, and one found higher levels in their coats (Vredegoor et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012; Nicholas et al., Am J Rhinol Allergy 2011). In the Vredegoor study, differences between breeds were small compared with differences between individual dogs of the same breed. The best approach is to spend time with the specific dog before making a commitment, and to talk to an allergist.

faq.q: Does bathing a dog reduce allergens?
faq.a: Yes, regular bathing can meaningfully reduce the amount of dander and allergen on a dog's coat and skin. Studies have shown that bathing a dog weekly can reduce airborne allergen levels in the home. Using a gentle, dog-appropriate shampoo is important to avoid drying out the skin, which can actually increase dander production. Keeping the dog out of the bedroom, using HEPA air purifiers, and vacuuming with a HEPA-filter vacuum are also highly effective strategies for managing dog allergens in the home.

Poodle mixes like Labradoodles, Goldendoodles, and Cockapoos are often marketed as hypoallergenic, but this is unreliable. Because they are crossbreeds, puppies can inherit the coat type of either parent — a Goldendoodle might have a tightly curled Poodle coat or a straight, heavy-shedding Golden Retriever coat. There is no way to guarantee which coat a mixed-breed puppy will have. If you specifically want a low-shedding dog, a purebred from a consistently low-shedding breed like the Poodle or Portuguese Water Dog is a more predictable choice than a Doodle mix, but a predictable coat does not mean lower allergen levels, so spend time with the individual dog first.
